description: Golden eval set for NutriBot. Expand to 30-50 items for tighter numbers. 'relevant_keywords' marks a retrieved chunk as relevant if it contains ANY listed keyword (case-insensitive) — a lightweight proxy for a human relevance label.

items.question: How much protein should I eat per day to build muscle?
items.expected_answer: Roughly 1.6 to 2.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day supports muscle growth for people doing resistance training.

items.question: What are good sources of dietary fiber?
items.expected_answer: Whole grains, legumes (beans, lentils), fruits, vegetables, nuts and seeds are high in dietary fiber.

items.question: Why is iron important and what foods are rich in it?
items.expected_answer: Iron is needed to make hemoglobin that carries oxygen in the blood. Red meat, poultry, beans, lentils, spinach and fortified cereals are iron-rich.

items.question: What does vitamin C do in the body?
items.expected_answer: Vitamin C supports the immune system, acts as an antioxidant, and helps the body absorb iron and produce collagen.

items.question: How do I lose weight in a healthy way?
items.expected_answer: Create a moderate calorie deficit through balanced eating and physical activity, aiming for gradual, sustainable weight loss rather than crash dieting.

items.question: What is the difference between saturated and unsaturated fats?
items.expected_answer: Saturated fats (mostly animal products) can raise LDL cholesterol; unsaturated fats (plant oils, nuts, fish) are generally healthier for the heart.

items.question: How much water should I drink each day?
items.expected_answer: General guidance is around 2 to 3 liters of fluids per day, varying with body size, activity level and climate.

items.question: What is calcium good for and where do I get it?
items.expected_answer: Calcium builds and maintains strong bones and teeth. Dairy, leafy greens, tofu and fortified foods are good sources.

items.question: Are carbohydrates bad for you?
items.expected_answer: Carbohydrates are the body's main energy source. Quality matters more than avoidance — favor whole grains, fruits and vegetables over refined sugars.

items.question: What foods help with a balanced healthy diet?
items.expected_answer: A balanced diet emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins and healthy fats while limiting added sugar, salt and processed foods.

items.question: What is vitamin D and why do I need it?
items.expected_answer: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bone health and supports immune function. It comes from sunlight, fatty fish and fortified foods.

items.question: How many calories are in one gram of fat versus protein?
items.expected_answer: Fat provides about 9 calories per gram, while protein and carbohydrates provide about 4 calories per gram.

items.question: What is potassium's role and what foods contain it?
items.expected_answer: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, fluid balance and muscle function. Bananas, potatoes, beans and leafy greens are good sources.

items.question: Is eating late at night bad for weight gain?
items.expected_answer: Total daily calorie intake matters more than timing; weight gain results from consistently eating more energy than you expend, regardless of the hour.

items.question: What are complete versus incomplete proteins?
items.expected_answer: Complete proteins contain all nine essential amino acids (mostly animal foods and soy); incomplete proteins lack one or more and can be combined from plant sources.
